title: CVC / Peel Natural Areas Inventory
description:
Natural Areas Inventories are designed to provide biological and ecological information that can be used to establish baseline conditions on natural heritage features and functions present at varying geographic scales, including at a project site, for an area or over a municipality or a watershed.

INSTRUCTIONS

Natural Area with Site Summaries are not visible when the map is first opened. To view, use the Zoom + button (or hold shift and drag a box) to bring up and navigate to Natural Areas which will be outlined in red. Click on a red Natural Area to bring up information in a pop-up window.

To view the Site Summary, Click on More info beside Link to Site Summary (PDF) in the pop-up window. The white Next feature arrow in the top right of the pop-up window will scroll through information pages for other related features. Additional navigation tools are located at the top of the map.

REPORTS

Credit River Watershed and Region of Peel NAI Report – Volume 1 (without Site Summaries)

A list of all Plants growing naturally in the study area.

A list of the Animals (birds, fish, butterflies, dragonflies/damselflies, reptiles, amphibians and mammals) in the study area.

Descriptions of Plant Communities in the study area.

Background Information on the project and on the study area (geology, physiography, soils, hydrology, human history, natural heritage and environmental management) and a description of the sections of the site summaries.

Additional details are available on a need-to-know basis by submitting a Data Request to the appropriate Conservation Authority. Email contact details are available for each Natural Area with Site Summary on the interactive map.

Requests for data on other natural areas in the Credit River watershed should be directed to CVC (Jacquelyn Kiers:
jkiers@creditvalleyca.ca). Requests for data on other natural areas in the Etobicoke Creek watershed, Mimico Creek watershed and Humber River watershed portions of the Region of Peel should be directed to TRCA (Susan Hayes:
SHayes@trca.on.ca).

This map is intended for illustration purposes only. The information shown should not be interpreted to represent the most up-to-date or accurate surveyed information.
snippet: A Natural Areas Inventory (NAI) is an inventory of the biological resources of a natural area – it documents the species and ecological features that are present in an area.
